speaker: Maera of Last Hearth
description: C1: Maera, who keeps Last Hearth - the hold-outs' and pilgrims' camp under the rim, the only people beyond it (faction hearthfolk; the seed of C4's settlement development). Before the giant has grown at the Rimstone she points it there; once it stands a colossus she asks it to clear the Rimward's engines from the Chainpit and to look out from the Hoarwatch (quest.rim_colossus); told it is done, she sets world.last_hearth.trials_told (the trials' last stage). Offended (faction.hearthfolk hostile), she takes 2 iron for the harm (outcome reconcile_hearthfolk). C4: her words follow the Hearth's tier (the hall roofed, the ring raised, the hold), and once the beacon burns she tells the watchers' sighting on the Hoarcrown's road (world.last_hearth.watchers_told: quest.hearth_frost_lead's first stage - a lead toward the Frostbound Titan, milestone D's); her board names what the Hearth needs. D1: once the watchers have gone up to the Rimeglass (lead.frostbound.hearth) she tells how the Frostbound is fought (his rime, the balefires, the ice under his weight); after his fall she hears it (outcome frost_fallen: world.last_hearth.frost_told, 200 XP) and tells the beacon's new sighting - the storm over the Drowned Steps (lead.stormcaller.hearth: quest.stormcaller_lead). D2: once the giant has looked south from the Breach's top (lead.stormcaller.seen) she tells what the pilgrims say of the Stormcaller (the bell-warden, his lightning, the water); after his fall she hears it (outcome storm_fallen: world.last_hearth.storm_told, 240 XP: the Lodestone stands below the beacon) and tells the rumour of Harrok's banner on the road again (lead.harrok.hearth: quest.harrok_lead - the lead toward his return, milestone E's).

nodes.text: Don't step - please - there are people under those tents. I am Maera; this is Last Hearth, what's left of the rim-folk who would not turn raider. We saw the rim split and the old stone wake. If you would be bigger still, go to the Rimstone on its rise, past the Fallen King. The stone hums at night. It is waiting for something your size. And if you would stay a while: the hall wants a roof-tree no man could lift. My tally-board by the fire says what the Hearth needs, and what it would give back.

Look at you. Our tents would not cover your foot. Then do what no one beyond the rim could: the Rimward hold the Chainpit with their engines and shoot at anything that moves on the causeway - break their engines (all three of them, or two at the least) with that new tread of yours, or simply stride over their ditches. And climb the Colossus Steps to the Hoarwatch: tell me what is moving on the Hoarcrown.

The engines are kindling and the Rimward are running for the passes. And the Hoarcrown? Frost on it in high summer, you say, and a shape in the ice... The stone will know you now. Go back to the Rimstone and grow.

Last Hearth will not forget whose shadow kept the raiders off. When the cold comes down from the Hoarcrown, we will be here - if you are. My tally-board by the fire says what the Hearth needs, and what it would give back.
Keep away! You crushed our tents - our people!
...Very well. Last Hearth forgives you. Watch where you put your feet.

Do you hear it? Children in the hall, and a fire that does not go out at night. The roof-tree you carried holds the turf like a mountain holds snow. The Rimward will have seen our smoke, mind - a roofed hall is worth burning. My tally-board by the fire says what the Hearth needs, and what it would give back.

Inside the ring we sleep. The archers on the steps say a man cannot climb your gate-stones and a raider cannot shift them. The smith has not stopped working since you set her anvil-stone. My tally-board by the fire says what the Hearth needs, and what it would give back.

A hold, now - with a beacon the Breach can see. The pilgrims are home. Whatever comes down from the Hoarcrown will find a fire burning and you beside it. My tally-board by the fire says what the Hearth needs, and what it would give back.

The beacon's watchers saw it two nights running: on the Hoarcrown's road, above the Hoarwatch, the snow lit from beneath - blue, then nothing - and the next morning the cairn the old kings built there was gone, and the ice below it split in a line as long as the causeway. Something that size does not walk. It comes down. Go and look from the Hoarwatch, and tell no one in the hold what you see until you know.

Three of mine went up past the Hoarwatch with all the pitch-pine they could drag, and they keep two balefires burning on the Rimeglass's shore. It is a tarn of black ice, and he kneels in it as if he grew there. The cold off him puts rime on your skin like frost on a blade - it will slow you, and if it closes on you, you will stand like a stone. Break it off with your own blows, or come to the fires. And watch his weight: the ice that holds you will not hold him if it is cracked.

The watchers' fires could see you from the beacon. When he went down the ice boomed all the way to the Hearth, and this morning the Rimeglass is water and floes - for the first time anyone remembers. My three are staying up there, by your leave; they want to raise the cairn again. And now listen. The beacon sees the other way too. Far south, over the rim and the Drowned Steps, there is a storm that has not moved in nine days, and lightning walks in it. Storms move. That one is waiting for something.

The Rimeglass is water and the watchers sleep warm. Look south, from the top of the Breach: the storm over the Drowned Steps has not moved. Whatever it is waiting for, it will be big enough to see you coming. My tally-board by the fire says what the Hearth needs, and what it would give back.

You saw it, then. The pilgrims who came up through the Old Kingdom say it sits over the top of the Drowned Steps, where the old kings flooded the road, and there is a giant standing in it with a rod taller than he is and a bell on his back. Lightning comes down where he points. The old songs call him the bell-warden. Mind the water up there: what strikes it runs through it, and it runs through whoever stands in it. A small body stands deep in a pool that a big one only wades. He stands in it too.

choices.text: Then I will make him stand in it.

nodes.text: We saw it from the beacon - the storm over the Steps broke and went to rags, and the sun came down on the water for the first time since the throne fell. The pilgrims say the Steps are only pools again. You brought me his stone? Then it stands by the Heart-ice, below the beacon, where the folk can touch it. And listen - the pilgrims bring something else up the road. Harrok's banner is out again in the Old Kingdom, and his clan is gathering at the Moot. Whatever you left between you there, it is not finished.

choices.text: Then I will look in at the Moot.

nodes.text: The Steps are calm, and the Lodestone still glows when thunder walks the hills. Harrok's banner is on the road; the Moot will tell you what it means. My tally-board by the fire says what the Hearth needs, and what it would give back.
